issues.description: PR description says CloseStream, code sends Close
issues.detail: The PR title and description repeatedly reference {"type": "CloseStream"} as the required control message, but the constant is _CLOSE_MSG = json.dumps({"type": "Close"}). Speak v1 and Listen v1 use different control message names. Verify against the Deepgram Speak v1 socket docs which token is correct; if Speak expects CloseStream, this fix sends the wrong string and the bug is not actually fixed. The data here is a tiny JSON string — get the shape right or the whole change is theater.

issues.description: Single receive() may not drain final messages
issues.detail: asyncio.wait_for(ws.receive(), timeout=1.0) reads exactly one frame, then closes. If Deepgram emits multiple final audio frames plus an acknowledgment, the close races them. A small loop reading until a close/ack frame or timeout would match the stated intent ("brief wait for final messages") more honestly. As written, the comment overstates what the code does.

except Exception catches CancelledError-adjacent and programming errors alongside the expected ConnectionResetError/ClientError. A narrower except (aiohttp.ClientError, ConnectionError, asyncio.TimeoutError) would say what is actually expected to fail during close. The finally: await ws.close() is correct and earns its keep; the except clause is the part doing too much.

issues.description: Constants belong with the class that uses them, but _close_ws lives on TTS
issues.detail: _FLUSH_MSG and _CLOSE_MSG are defined on SynthesizeStream, but the only caller in the diff is TTS._close_ws referencing SynthesizeStream._FLUSH_MSG. That cross-class reach is mild code smell — either move the constants to module scope (two strings, two lines, no class needed) or put _close_ws on the class that owns the protocol. Data dominates: these are just two JSON strings; they don't need a class.

review.summary: Small, well-shaped fix — the change is right-sized and the finally-close pattern is correct. The data is two JSON strings and a one-second wait; that's the whole problem. My main concern is a possible wrong-string bug: the PR description says CloseStream but the code sends Close. Verify which token Speak v1 actually expects before merging — if it's wrong, this fix doesn't fix anything. Secondary nits: the receive() reads one frame and claims to drain \"final messages,\" the except Exception is broader than the failure modes warrant, and the constants don't need to live on the class.
